LESSON: WRITING 11.4.1 SPELLING: SYNONYMS AND ANTONYMS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Writing 11.4.1 Spelling: Synonyms and Antonyms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.4.1 Spelling: Synonyms and Antonyms, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words? 2) How do you identify synonyms and antonyms correctly in a sentence?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify synonyms and antonyms correctly for writing fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.4.1 Spelling: Synonyms and Antonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use synonyms and antonyms correctly in sentences,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 11.4.1 Spelling: Synonyms and Antonyms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. advocate the use of a rich vocabulary in writing. ● Learner with low vision is guided watch while learners with blindness listen to an audio-visual recording or listen to sentences read by the teacher and identify words with synonyms and antonyms. ● In pairs, learners are guided to form sentences using synonyms and antonyms. ● In groups, learners are guided to identify synonyms and antonyms from braille/appropriate print newspapers, magazines or the internet using digital devices with assistive technology and use them to construct sentences. ● Learners are guided to write the sentence on a braille/print chart with appropriate font size and colour contrast and display their work in class. 1) How do you tell the meaning of unfamiliar words? 2) How do you identify synonyms and antonyms correctly in a sentence? 70

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.4.1 Spelling: Synonyms and Antonyms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
Unity and love: promoted as learners suggest synonyms and

antonyms and then use them to form sentences in pairs or small

groups.

Link to other learning areas:

Synonyms and antonyms are learnt in all languages.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Digital devices with assistive technology

● Print charts with appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille charts with synonym and antonym
